issue.title: Recalibrate the scoped lane's serial-runtime budget against real lane history
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-gj.2 and sase-gj.7 while the diff-scoped lane latency epic was in flight; corroborated with new measurements by the sase-gj land agent.

FULL_LANE_WALL_SECONDS (tests/_test_selection_health.py) is 232.0s and doubles as the default for SASE_TEST_SELECTION_MAX_SERIAL_SECONDS, i.e. the crossover at which RULE_SERIAL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED escalates or hands a selection to the middle gear. It was set from a single 2026-08-06 measurement at 28 workers. Three later same-day timed full lanes on the same host came in well under it: 159.0s (sase-gj.7, 26,497 tests), and 139.95s during the sase-gj land verification (26,496 passed / 7 skipped). If that holds, the budget is ~1.5x looser than the real crossover, so runs that should escalate or engage the gear stay serial.

sase-gj.2 separately proposed correcting the duration table for parallel contention: per-test seconds recorded on the 28-worker full lane over-state an isolated serial run (hand samples: 12 slow ACE files estimated 338.8s vs 298.2s actual, 1.14x; 11 selection-test files 26.4s vs 11.8s, 2.2x). That measurement does NOT reproduce against real lane history, which is the evidence sase-gj.2 wanted and could not get at the time: the health store does record manifest["selected"], timings.estimated_serial_seconds, and the run duration together on every non-escalated schema>=6 record. Estimate/actual over the 4 such serial records now in the store is mean 0.90x (0.74, 0.91, 0.92, 1.03) — the estimate slightly UNDER-states real lane wall clock, because the lane duration also carries pytest startup and the contract set. n=4 is thin; the two measurements disagree and need more samples to settle.

Also of note: the merged table total moved from 4268.4s over 2346 files (sase-gj.1) to 3239.0s over 2370 files (land), so the table itself is load-sensitive between recordings.

Scope: take repeated timed full-lane measurements, pull estimate-vs-duration pairs from the accumulated store, decide whether FULL_LANE_WALL_SECONDS should move and whether the per-file table needs a contention correction, and update the constants, their "measured, deliberately constant" docstrings, and docs/development.md with the new numbers. Do not change the constant on a single sample; that is what produced this task.

payload.entry: Backlog triage (owner-requested seven-bead cut, 2026-08-12): this was already snoozed to 2026-08-14 rather than triaged. The evidence is 'the constant may be ~1.5x loose', with the bead's own analysis noting the two measurements disagree (estimate/actual mean 0.90x over n=4) and that the table itself is load-sensitive between recordings. No agent has reported a scoped lane that stayed serial when it should have escalated. sase-j0 stays open for the same 'a committed perf budget no longer matches reality' problem on the test-cost budgets, which is actually red; whoever lands that recalibration methodology should re-file this with a +1 if the scoped-lane budget still looks wrong afterward.

payload.close_reason: Deferred budget recalibration; not among the owner's seven, and no observed mis-escalation
